# Your Friday in St. Louis (Oct 30)

It's Halloween eve, so the city will be lively.

**Late morning: The Griot Museum of Black History** (Old North St. Louis)
A small, deeply personal museum with life-size figures of Black Missourians most people never learned about. It's a real local gem. Check the hours, since they're limited.

**Lunch: Smoki O's** (North Broadway)
Get the rib tips and a **snoot**, crispy fried pig snout, a true St. Louis soul food staple most visitors never hear of. It runs on lunch hours, so go early.

**Afternoon: A slow drive through The Ville**
Pass **Sumner High School**, the first Black high school west of the Mississippi. Tina Turner, Chuck Berry, Arthur Ashe and **Dick Gregory**, the original king of comedy, all went there. Annie Malone's Poro College empire was also in this neighborhood.

**Evening: Comedy**
Check **Helium** or **The Funny Bone** for Halloween-weekend headliners. It's a big weekend for touring Black comics.
